title: Learning personalities by probing
question: Can a deliberate single-region probe in round 1 make τ learnable from the national poll, and is the exploration worth its price?

metric_definitions.tau_by_round[t]: decision point t+1: statistics of the τ values of the accepted worlds among D candidates (σ ~ posterior, τ uniform over 24 permutations) that match every poll s ≤ t+1 within 2.5·(SE_s + 0.01)
metric_definitions.H_perm: plug-in entropy (nats) of the accepted τ over the 24 permutations (prior ln 24 = 3.178)
metric_definitions.H_soft / *_soft / ess_soft: secondary, 'what the polls could teach': the D candidates weighted by the Gaussian poll likelihood Π_s N(p̂_s; E_w(s), SE_s²) WITHOUT the 0.01 slack (soft Bayesian posterior over τ; ess = 1/Σw² effective sample size)
metric_definitions.H_marginal_mean: mean over regions of the entropy of the accepted personality of that region (prior ln 4 = 1.386)
metric_definitions.H_probe_region: the same for the region the probe player probed in that seed (all arms use it)
metric_definitions.p_true_tau: fraction of accepted worlds with exactly the true τ (prior 1/24 = 0.042)
metric_definitions.p_true_tau_r_mean / p_true_tau_probe_reg: fraction with the true personality of a region (prior 0.25)
metric_definitions.guaranteed_by_round: K_p(Guaranteed) = ∃π∀w win over 16 poll-consistent worlds (logic.report timeline)
metric_definitions.expected / victory: deterministic expected share E at the election; official sampled vote > N/2

deviations: Added a control arm poll_planner (BayesPlanner with poll-consistent planning worlds): the plain BayesPlanner never conditions its planning worlds on the polls, so without the control the probe arm would change two things at once (probing and using the polls).

τ learning is measured with D = 512 candidate worlds per game replayed once through the whole history (acceptance at every t from the recorded shares) instead of calling consistent_worlds at each t; this is the same rule and the same keys (library_check compares the accepted count at t = T with consistent_worlds). σ for these worlds is drawn from the posterior at t = T (all queries); σ entropy is ≈ 0 after the survey (seed_info / tau_learning), so this does not affect τ.

The probe score is a discriminability ratio (between-τ_r variance of the predicted round-2 poll over SE² + within variance), a monotone proxy for the expected information about τ_r from one Gaussian poll.
World micro-states are drawn by the library sampler (sample_worlds) on CPU generators and moved to cuda:2; replays, rollouts and the probe scoring run on the GPU.
